sections.what: `engine/items/use_actions.py` decides whether an item can be used by counting `triggers` edges, not by reading `properties.triggers`. Line 135 sets `has_any_trigger = len(get_edges_for_source(item_node.id, EDGE_TRIGGERS)) > 0`, and lines 356 to 369 scan the same edges for an `on_use_on` trigger. After the task-886 migration an item whose triggers live in the property array has zero edges, so `use` is refused for any item that does not also list `use` in `actions`, and `use X on Y` is refused for every authored `on_use_on` rule. Measured on HEAD mansion.json: 4 definitions on 3 items (`item_granola_bar`, `item_water_bottle`, `item_unlabeled_vial`) have an `on_use` property trigger and no `use` action, so all three regress to "you can't use that" after migration.
sections.why: The trigger engine already fires property triggers; only the permission guard looks at the retired store. A player can hold an item with an authored use trigger and be told they cannot use it. The `on_use_on` case is the key-in-lock pattern the docs recommend authoring, and it breaks the same way the first time anyone authors one.
sections.how: Add one helper to the trigger system that answers "does this node have a trigger of type T", reading `(node.properties or {}).get('triggers')` first (accepting a string, a list or an entry with `id`) plus legacy edges, and use it in both guards. Do not duplicate the trigger-type normalisation three times; one function, both call sites. Keep the existing edge path so a pre-migration world still works.
sections.verify:
1. Drive `use` on an item whose only `on_use` rule lives in `properties.triggers` and which has no `use` action.
   - expected: the use is accepted and the trigger runs.
   - observed: `test_use_is_allowed_by_an_on_use_property_trigger` calls `world.use_item` and gets a result string; before the change the guard raised `ValueError` because it counted `triggers` edges only.
2. Drive `use X on Y` for a pair whose `on_use_on` rule lives only in the property array.
   - expected: accepted, and the same pair with only a legacy edge is still accepted.
   - observed: `test_use_on_is_allowed_by_an_on_use_on_property_trigger` and `test_use_on_still_reads_the_legacy_edge_store` both pass.
3. Drive `use` on an item with no action and no trigger.
   - expected: still refused, so the guard has not become unconditional.
   - observed: `test_use_is_refused_without_any_trigger_or_action` raises `ValueError`.
4. Run the targeted suites the card names.
   - expected: pass.
   - observed: `python -m pytest tests/test_consume_contract.py tests/test_trigger_system.py tests/test_use_trigger_guard.py tests/test_trigger_migration.py tests/test_trigger_materialize.py` reports 182 passed. The named scenario items (`item_granola_bar`, `item_unlabeled_vial`) were not driven through the live app: it has not been restarted since the engine edit, so the running process still holds the pre-fix guard. The guard's mechanism is proven by fixtures; its live behaviour on those two items is left for the reviewer's restarted check.

acceptance.text: use on an item with an on_use property trigger and no use action succeeds (synthetic fixture; the named `item_granola_bar` is not driven live, see step 4)
use on an item with two on_use property triggers runs both (fixture covers the multi-entry read; execution order is the existing trigger runner)
use key on door succeeds for an item whose on_use_on rule lives only in properties.triggers
The same item with only a legacy triggers edge still succeeds
The guard reports false when the node has neither a property trigger nor an edge
